articles.title: “I had to stop”: Travis Kelce mother Donna Kelce opens up on the dream she gave up to raise him and Jason Kelce
articles.summary: Travis Kelce, the Kansas City Chiefs’ tight end, and his brother, the former Philadelphia Eagles’ icon Jason Kelce, have established multiple businesses
articles.body: Travis Kelce, the Kansas City Chiefs’ tight end, and his brother, the former Philadelphia Eagles’ icon Jason Kelce, have established multiple businesses together after having successful careers on the field. Both Travis Kelce and Jason Kelce have also been public about how much their parents, Ed Kelce and Donna Kelce, have supported them through all the difficult phases in their lives. Amid the new season, Travis Kelce and Jason Kelce’s mother, Donna Kelce, has reflected on how she gave up on her dreams for her children.Travis Kelce and Jason Kelce’s mother Donna Kelce reflects on the dream she had to give up for themIn an interview on Kylie Kelce’s popular podcast, Not Gonna Lie, Travis Kelce and Jason Kelce’s mother Donna Kelce said, “I did learn how to be a pilot before I had children…”Travis Kelce and Jason Kelce’s mother Donna Kelce added, “I actually went up and flew a plane…”Soon after learning how to fly, priorities changes for Travis Kelce and Jason Kelce’s parents, Ed and Donna Kelce.Donna Kelce added, “I did, but we wanted to have children, and it was really expensive, so I had to stop…Ed and I decided, well, we should probably get a house and start having kids.”To this, Jason Kelce’s wife Kylie Kelce added, "That is so cool! Does Jason know that?"Donna Kelce responded as, "I don't know if he knows it or not — I don't know if I've ever really brought it up," she said, laughing.Travis Kelce and Jason Kelce’s parents and especially, their mother, Donna Kelce, has been a driving force behind their successful careers both on and off the field.In many of their interviews, both Travis Kelce and his older brother, Jason Kelce, have spoken about how Donna Kelce has been a strong source of strength and support to both of them.While there has been a considerable amount of buzz around Travis Kelce’s personal life, Donna Kelce has kept things private and has always respected the privacy he wants to have in his life.Travis Kelce and Jason Kelce’s bond could be attributed to how Donna Kelce raised them bothMany have also praised Donna Kelce for the bond that Travis Kelce and Jason Kelce share with one another.Despite playing in rival teams, both Travis Kelce and his older brother Jason Kelce have always shared a close bond with one another and have remained the best of friends with each other.After retiring from the league, Jason Kelce joined Travis Kelce on a number of ventures together as their podcast, New Heights, has been highly successful and recently, signed a $100 million deal with Amazon.For now, the focus remains on Travis Kelce as he breaks records on the field.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: "Tom has kept his distance from falling in love": Tom Brady reportedly avoids serious with Candice Swanepoel after Gisele Bündchen heartbreak
articles.summary: Tom Brady and Candice Swanepoel may be enjoying their new romance, but reports suggest they have different expectations about where it could lead.
articles.body: Tom Brady and Candice Swanepoel may be enjoying their new romance, but reports suggest they have different expectations about where it could lead. The retired NFL quarterback, who has kept his personal life relatively private since his divorce from Gisele Bündchen, is reportedly in no rush to make things official. Swanepoel, meanwhile, appears more comfortable bringing their relationship into the public eye. Their reported differences have already sparked questions about whether the two are looking for the same kind of commitment.Tom Brady and Candice Swanepoel reportedly have different relationship expectationsBrady and Swanepoel reportedly began seeing each other in June, although news of their relationship only surfaced last weekend. Both are based in Miami, where they are said to have kept their meetings discreet for several months.However, a source cited by the Daily Mail claims the relationship may be moving at different speeds for the two stars. While Swanepoel reportedly wants something more serious, Brady appears content with keeping things casual.“Candice is definitely the one who has been more eager to get this relationship out there, while Tom is happy to enjoy what they have without putting too much of a label on it,” the source said.The insider also suggested that Brady has no plans to publicly embrace a serious relationship anytime soon.“He’s not going to broadcast it anytime soon because he enjoys being known as the bachelor,” the source continued. “His relationship mindset only makes the women he does hook up with want him more because they want to attain what might be unattainable.”At 49, Brady has attracted attention for his romantic life since ending his marriage to Bündchen in 2022. Swanepoel, 38, also has a family of her own, sharing two sons with her former fiancé, Hermann Nicoli. Brady has three children from his relationships with Bündchen and Bridget Moynahan.Tom Brady's priorities reportedly remain family and Fox broadcasting careerBrady's approach to dating may have a lot to do with how he has chosen to organise his life after his divorce. According to the insider, the seven-time Super Bowl champion has avoided serious romantic commitments while focusing on his children and professional responsibilities.“Since Gisele, Tom has kept his distance from falling in love and has instead had flings or hookups because his kids and his job are what is important to him,” the source said. “He knows relationships come and go, but family and football are forever, and he isn’t interested in heartache.”His broadcasting career with Fox Sports is also reportedly taking priority over settling down again.“His priority is his career, and the idea of settling into a committed relationship just isn’t at the top of his to-do list,” the insider said, adding that it could “change down the road.”Meanwhile, the reported romance has attracted additional attention following comments from fellow model Joan Smalls, who was previously linked to Brady and seemingly called Swanepoel a “backstabber.”Brady reportedly wants to stay away from the tension. For now, whether his relationship with Swanepoel develops into something more serious remains uncertain. Neither has publicly confirmed the reported differences in their expectations.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: George Kittle and wife Claire win hearts with emotional Iowa Children’s Hospital visit
articles.summary: George Kittle has never forgotten the people and places that shaped his journey.
articles.body: George Kittle has never forgotten the people and places that shaped his journey. Before returning to the spotlight at Iowa’s Kinnick Stadium, the San Francisco 49ers tight end chose to make a difference away from the football field. Alongside his wife, Claire, Kittle visited young patients at the University of Iowa Stead Family Children’s Hospital. Their visit brought smiles to children facing difficult days and highlighted a charitable commitment that has remained close to the couple’s hearts throughout his NFL career.George Kittle and Claire bring smiles to young patients at Iowa Children’s HospitalWith the 49ers enjoying their bye week, Kittle returned to his former college town ahead of Iowa’s home game. However, his first priority was not football. He and Claire spent time with children receiving treatment at the University of Iowa Stead Family Children’s Hospital, creating special moments through conversations, laughter and simple gestures of kindness.The visit also reflected the couple’s plans to make hospital outreach a regular part of their charitable work through the Kittle Fund. Their foundation aims to support children battling illnesses, animal shelters and military veterans.Speaking about the inspiration behind their efforts on The Rich Eisen Show, Kittle explained how his connection with the hospital began during his college years.“Claire and I have done a bunch of community work my entire career going back to college. I think a big part of that started with the University of Iowa and the Iowa Children’s Hospital,” said Kittle.He also recalled how visiting young patients became an important part of his experience as an Iowa athlete.“Being athletes there, like we always got to do like community service stuff, go through the hospital and hang out with kids. And I think that just really stuck with us throughout my NFL career. And so the whole point of it is like our motto is we want to show up for those who show up for us.”George Kittle prepares for special role as Iowa honorary captainKittle’s return to Iowa also carries a special football connection. The former Hawkeye is set to serve as the team's honorary captain for its home game against Northwestern. He will join the team captains at midfield for the coin toss and spend time with the players in the locker room.His relationship with the children's hospital stretches back several years. In 2023, Kittle and Claire visited young patients, playing video games, signing autographs and spending time with their families. He also returned in 2019 alongside former Iowa teammate C.J. Beathard.Kittle has supported the hospital through fundraising efforts as well. He previously auctioned a specially designed championship belt signed by several NFL tight ends, with the proceeds benefiting young patients.For Kittle, returning to Iowa means more than celebrating his college football roots. It is also an opportunity to give back to a community that helped shape him, both as an athlete and as a person.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: From children's hospitals to community causes: Josh Allen and Hailee Steinfeld's millions in charity-linked support
articles.summary: Josh Allen and Hailee Steinfeld have plenty to celebrate in their personal lives, but their charitable work offers another reason they continue to attract
articles.body: Josh Allen and Hailee Steinfeld have plenty to celebrate in their personal lives, but their charitable work offers another reason they continue to attract attention. The Buffalo Bills quarterback has built a strong connection with children's healthcare in Western New York, turning personal loss into a long-running effort to help families. Steinfeld, meanwhile, has used her celebrity platform to support children's hospitals and several charitable causes. Their contributions tell two different stories, but both highlight how public figures can use their influence to make a difference beyond their careers.Josh Allen's $17,000 donation started a much bigger charitable movementOne of Allen's most meaningful charitable contributions came in November 2020, following the death of his grandmother, Patricia Allen. Bills supporters began donating to John R. Oishei Children's Hospital in her memory, with many choosing $17 contributions to honour the quarterback's jersey number.The response quickly gathered momentum. When the donations approached $500,000, Allen personally pledged another $17,000 to help push the total higher. More than 23,000 contributions had already reached the hospital.The donations eventually led to the creation of the Patricia Allen Fund in December 2020. According to the hospital foundation, the fund was established with input from Allen and his family to support children receiving critical care.This became one of the most important parts of his charitable work. Instead of making a single contribution and moving on, Allen continued supporting the hospital through different campaigns and fundraising efforts.Josh Allen's other donations include a $100,000 pledge with NikeAllen had already been supporting children's healthcare before his grandmother's passing.In 2019, he committed to donating $200 to Oishei Children's Hospital for every touchdown he scored or threw. His contribution reached $10,000 by the end of the season. He also designed a limited-edition New Era cap with hospital patients and staff, with part of the sales proceeds benefiting the hospital.His involvement continued through the NFL's My Cause My Cleats campaign. Allen worked with two young patients, Charlie and Clayton, to create custom footwear. He later put the cleats up for auction, directing the proceeds towards Oishei Children's Hospital.In December 2021, Allen and Nike announced a joint $100,000 pledge to the hospital. The contribution supported patient treatment and reflected his desire to give back to the community that welcomed him after he entered the NFL.Another notable contribution came in May 2024. Allen agreed to donate $117,000 to Oishei Children's Hospital through the 117 Holes for Children's fundraising event. The money supported the Patricia Allen Fund, and he encouraged fans to match his contribution.The event eventually raised $775,000, including Allen's personal pledge.Josh Allen's $2 million charity milestone involved West Herr and New EraAllen's charitable influence has also helped bring major corporate contributions to Buffalo.In October 2022, West Herr Auto Group donated $2,000,017 to the Patricia Allen Fund. Allen attended the announcement at Oishei Children's Hospital, but the contribution came from the automotive company, not his personal finances.The additional $17 honoured his jersey number and the campaign's connection to his grandmother.His partnership with New Era has also produced impressive results. The Billustration campaign invited young patients at Golisano Children's Hospital to design special caps that Allen wore before Bills home games.The first campaign raised $140,230 through nine cap auctions in 2025. In May 2026, New Era and Allen celebrated the success by releasing a special edition cap featuring the children's designs. Every purchase benefited the Patricia Allen Fund.The initiative returned for 2026 with eight new designs created by young patients. It gave children a creative opportunity while directing more support towards families receiving hospital care.Other contributions included EA Sports' $10,000 donation to the Patricia Allen Fund in 2023, announced when Allen appeared on the Madden NFL 24 cover.These figures should not all be counted as Allen's personal donations. They demonstrate how his involvement has encouraged businesses, fans and partners to contribute.Hailee Steinfeld's charitable work includes a children's hospital campaignSteinfeld's public charitable record is less focused on large personal cash donations, but she has participated in several initiatives.One of her best-documented campaigns dates back to July 2017, when she partnered with MISSION to launch the What's Your Mission? T-shirt initiative.The campaign supported Children's Hospital Los Angeles, with $5 from every T-shirt purchase going towards the hospital.The actress and singer also spoke about her connection with the organisation and her interest in helping children and families who need medical support.Her charitable affiliations extend beyond that campaign. Public charity profiles have associated her with organisations including St. Jude Children's Research Hospital, UNICEF, the American Cancer Society, the Leukemia & Lymphoma Society, Project Sunshine, Ronald McDonald House Charities, Stand Up To Cancer and the Children's Defense Fund.However, these affiliations should not be mistaken for confirmed personal cash donations to every organisation.There has also been a report claiming that Steinfeld donated $100,000 to Ella Thompson, a young Buffalo Bills fan reportedly battling stage 4 neuroblastoma, in October 2025. However, an independently verifiable fundraising record or reliable confirmation of the contribution remains unavailable. The amount should therefore be treated as an unverified report rather than an established donation.Josh Allen and Hailee Steinfeld's generosity extends beyond financial contributionsThe couple's generosity has also appeared in smaller personal gestures.In December 2025, Allen and Steinfeld reportedly gave Buffalo Bills offensive linemen a quarter of a cow each as a Christmas present. Allen also included an infrared steak searer to help his teammates prepare the meat.The gifts were shared publicly by the wife of offensive tackle Alec Anderson. While this was not a charitable donation, it offered a glimpse into the couple's thoughtful approach to personal relationships.Their public records show different approaches to giving. Allen has developed a long-term relationship with children's healthcare organisations, particularly through the Patricia Allen Fund. Steinfeld has supported charitable campaigns and used her platform to bring attention to causes affecting children and families.There is no independently confirmed combined donation total for the couple. Still, Allen's ongoing hospital work and Steinfeld's charitable partnerships show that their influence reaches beyond football, music and Hollywood.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Tom Brady drops another 'oh s***' live on Fox during appearance on 'Fox NFL Sunday'
articles.summary: Tom Brady is now a repeat offender when it comes to using foul language on live TV.
articles.body:
Legendary NFL quarterback Tom Brady is still getting a hang of this broadcasting thing. While Brady has worked hard to improve as a broadcaster over the years, there's still one area in which he could clean up: his foul language.

For the second time this season, Brady dropped an "oh s***" while live on Fox. This time around, his NSFW moment occurred during an appearance on "Fox NFL Sunday," where he was pulled into a trivia segment with Drew Brees.

The segment focused on Brady and Brees trying to name the quarterback who ranked third all-time behind them in significant stat categories. Upon giving an incorrect answer, Brady uttered "oh s***" before quickly realizing his mistake.

The desk very clearly heard Brady's mistake and saw his reaction. After a few members at the desk laughed, host Curt Menefee eventually said, "We let you get away with one, by the way. We heard you. That's OK."

Menefee then ended the segment, but both he and Michael Strahan still got in one more reference to Brady's slip-up. After Strahan mentioned the program was live, Menefee said, "[Brady's] learning."

The former quarterback may need to do a better job drilling that particular rule into his head. Sunday marked the second time this season in which Brady was caught using that expletive on the air.

His first use of that phrase came back in Week 2, when Washington Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels dislocated his left elbow. Upon seeing a replay of the play , Brady — who was in the booth calling the game — uttered "oh s***" after he saw Daniels' elbow bend the wrong way.

Brady quickly apologized for that incident, saying he "was not expecting to see that."

Following his Week 8 gaffe, Brady will call the Detroit Lions vs. Minnesota Vikings game, where he'll look to practice some language discipline after his early mistake.

articles.title: Lamar Jackson ruled out of Bills-Ravens game with thumb injury sustained on Baltimore's first offensive play
articles.summary: Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson left Sunday's game against the Buffalo Bills with an apparent injury on Buffalo's first offensive play.
articles.body:
Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson left Sunday's game against the Buffalo Bills with a right thumb injury sustained on Baltimore's first offensive play from scrimmage.

The Ravens quickly ruled him out for the rest of the game.

Jackson took contact on his hand after a pass and was in immediate pain. He left the field and walked straight to the locker room. Backup Tyler Huntley took his place at quarterback.

The Ravens initially announced that Jackson was questionable to return with a thumb injury before ruling him out before the conclusion of the first quarter. The injury is to the thumb on his throwing hand.

Jackson, a two-time NFL MVP, was playing in his first game since sustaining a high-ankle sprain in Week 4 that caused him to miss three games. He returned to the 4-3 Ravens in time for the critical AFC showdown against Josh Allen and the Bills, but now he's out against the Bills and potentially for longer.

The injury is another difficult blow for Jackson and a Ravens team seeking to compete for a Super Bowl championship. Jackson is one of the game's best players when healthy, but injuries have derailed his last two seasons.

Jackson missed four games last season and was limited in several others with leg and back injuries. The Ravens were projected last season as a Super Bowl contender but finished 8-9 and missed the playoffs.

The Ravens again were projected to compete for a Super Bowl this season, but Jackson is now potentially looking at a long-term absence. Jackson, 29, is playing on the fourth year of a five-year, $260 million contract.

Team owner Steve Bisciotti has expressed his desire to make Jackson a Raven for life, but the two sides reportedly haven't engaged in substantial contract negotiations .

articles.title: “Is This Kid a Joke”: Ex-Jets HC Blasts Ashton Jeanty on Live TV After Raiders RB’s Dig at New York
articles.summary: Former New York Jets head coach Rex Ryan lost his cool on live television in the build-up to Week 8. Ryan went on a rant during ESPN’s Sunday NFL Countdown a...
articles.body:
Former New York Jets head coach Rex Ryan lost his cool on live television in the build-up to Week 8. Ryan went on a rant during ESPN's Sunday NFL Countdown after Las Vegas Raiders 2nd-year running back Ashton Jeanty said that a few New York defenders don't want to make tackles.

The incident happened on Wednesday as the 3-4 Raiders were set to face the 2-5 Jets at MetLife Stadium. Jeanty, who had a poor 15-yard performance on 8 carries against the Rams, told reporters about the Jets' defense, "I think we can definitely get the run game going. Get back on track and really get after these guys. A couple guys out there that don't really want to tackle, but I'm not going to say names."

This comment got to Rex Ryan, who defended his team's linebacker Demario Davis on ESPN.

"You know who hand-picked this guy when he came out of college? You're looking at him. Why? Because he knocked your face in! Is this kid a joke or what? Does he not look at the tape? Because when I see the tape, I see that. I see Demario Davis not losing a step, still playing at the top of his game. But you know what else I see? How about Mr. Tiptoe Through the Tulips, avoiding contact. This guy is soft as Charmin. Look at him. Oh, hired killer right there," Rex Ryan said on ESPN's Coach's Clicker.

Davis was drafted in the third round of the 2012 NFL Draft by the Jets. At that time, Ryan was the head coach of the franchise and a major driving force for Davis' selection. Ryan famously compared him to Hall of Famer Ray Lewis.

So, as Ryan stood next to Tedy Bruschi at the touchscreen, Ryan discussed the footage. Whilst showing Demario Davis making big hits, Ryan pointed out how Jeanty was leaning away from the contact to avoid tackles. He made his point clear that Jeanty had no right to question how physical Gang Green are.

"Look, I'm gonna tell you something, Bru. I'm gonna talk to this kid before the game. I'm going right up to him. You know me, I tell the truth. I'm going right up to him, and I say, 'Listen young man, I heard what you said. And I want you to know something, all right? We are not going to try to take you out of the game…Why? Because you are horrible. You're about the worst draft pick in the last 20 years, I think, as a running back. You stink. You're averaging 3.1 yards a carry. And guess what? Today you get your a– kicked, and you know who else does? Your teammates. It's on you, my friend.'"

When asked by Bruschi if he would go right up to him, Ryan said, "Right up to his a–." Ryan said that Jeanty's poor running was holding Las Vegas back in their four-game losing streak and his comments would weigh heavily on him Sunday.

articles.title: Colts' early-round draft pick makes first start v. Jaguars
articles.summary: Indianapolis Colts' rookie linebacker CJ Allen is making his first NFL start against the Jacksonville Jaguars in Week 8.
articles.body:
Indianapolis Colts' rookie linebacker CJ Allen is making his first NFL start against the Jacksonville Jaguars in Week 8.

Earlier in the week, defensive coordinator Lou Anarumo strongly hinted that this would be the case. Allen did not play last week against Minnesota due to injury, but Anarumo said if he had been available, he would have started in that game as well.

Anarumo added that Allen will be the middle linebacker, although Akeem Davis-Gaither will continue to wear the green dot as the defensive signal caller.

Allen was a second-round pick by the Colts this past April, and the expectation early on was that he would start right away and wear the green dot. However, after missing time during training camp, that never came to fruition.

Instead, Allen's role as a rookie had been relatively small. While the Colts rotated heavily at the WILL linebacker position, Allen was specifically a MIKE, a role filled by Davis-Gaither, who Anarumo did not want to take off the field.

So through seven games, Allen had played only 48 defensive snaps, which includes not seeing the field at all in two contests, even though he was healthy.

articles.title: Steelers respond to 'dirty' comments from Browns' Jared Verse with in-game scrap
articles.summary: The Browns defensive end was slammed to the ground by the Steelers' left guard in the first quarter at Acrisure Stadium.
articles.body:
Cam Heyward's promise that the Steelers would "address" trash talk by Cleveland Browns defensive end Jared Verse came true during their pivotal NFL Week 8 meeting Nov. 1 at Acrisure Stadium.

Left guard Mason McCormick slammed Verse to the ground on an extra point attempt following Rico Dowdle's touchdown that put Pittsburgh up 7-0 in the first quarter.

McCormick was flagged for unnecessary roughness on the play. Verse was not penalized but was seen celebrating as he and his Cleveland teammates ran off the field after the play.

The penalty ended up not hurting the Steelers, as Cleveland was forced to punt on the subsequent drive.

"They were talking crazy," Verse told reporters in his post-game news conference after the teams' Week 4 meeting in early October. "I was telling them, 'Y'all double-teaming and sliding and you're garbage.' I don't have respect for anybody that plays too dirty and does too much extra [stuff] after the game. I can't wait to see them again. It's going to be a great time when I see them again."

That apparently did not sit well with the Steelers, especially considering they dropped a 27-24 decision in overtime during their trip to Cleveland on Oct. 2

Heyward said as much in an appearance on the Rich Eisen Show on Oct. 29 in anticipation of the rematch that will decide control of the AFC North division.

"Double teaming, sliding, chipping, are those not allowed in our game?" Heyward said Tuesday on The Rich Eisen show. "Yeah, I got the bruises to prove it. But we don't whine about it, baby. It's part of the game. And so, I'm looking forward to this game. It's gonna be a fun game. Both teams are in position to do a lot of work in this division, as they say.

Who are the scariest players in NFL history? These are our choices.

"The AFC North is on fire and I'm glad I'm in the kitchen because I like it that way. But those are words that were said and they will be addressed."

The Steelers and Browns are fighting for first place in the division. The winning team will take the lead at 6-2. Cincinnati enters the week a half game behind both teams at 4-2.

articles.title: Raiders score NFL's first kickoff return touchdown of 2026
articles.summary: The Jets moved back into the lead on a second quarter touchdown, but their edge over the Raiders did not last long.
articles.body:
The Jets moved back into the lead on a second quarter touchdown, but their edge over the Raiders did not last long.

Dylan Laube returned the ensuing kickoff for a 95-yard touchdown. It is the first kickoff return touchdown in the NFL this season and it has the Raiders up 14-13 with just over 10 minutes to play in the first half.

Geno Smith hit wide receiver Isaiah Williams for an 18-yard touchdown to cap an eight-play, 70-yard drive and give the Jets their brief 13-7 lead.

Smith completed three other passes for 45 yards on the drive and the one incompletion was a drop of a well-thrown deep ball. Wide receiver Adonai Mitchell was responsible for that drop, but redeemed himself with a pair of catches for 41 yards later in the drive.
